words.definition: n. the organic chemistry of compounds and processes occurring in organisms; the effort to understand biology within the context of chemistry

examples.en: Advances in [biochemistry] have enabled scientists to develop targeted drug therapies for genetic diseases.
examples.cn: [生物化学]的进步使科学家能够开发针对遗传疾病的靶向药物疗法。

examples.en: She majored in [biochemistry] and wrote her dissertation on the role of enzymes in metabolic disorders.
examples.cn: 她主修[生物化学]，并就酶在代谢疾病中的作用撰写了毕业论文。

examples.en: The [biochemistry] of human digestion involves complex sequences of chemical reactions in the stomach and intestines.
examples.cn: 人类消化的[生物化学]涉及胃和肠道中复杂的化学反应序列。

examples.en: Understanding [biochemistry] at the molecular level is essential for the development of new pharmaceutical compounds.
examples.cn: 在分子水平上理解[生物化学]对新型药物化合物的开发至关重要。

examples.en: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry has frequently been awarded for breakthroughs in [biochemistry] and molecular biology.
examples.cn: 诺贝尔化学奖多次授予[生物化学]和分子生物学领域的突破性成果。

words.translation: n. 传记
words.definition: n. an account of the series of events making up a person's life

examples.en: The [biography] of Marie Curie reveals a life defined by intellectual brilliance and personal sacrifice.
examples.cn: 玛丽·居里的[传记]揭示了一个以卓越才智和个人牺牲为特征的人生。

examples.en: He spent four years researching archival documents before completing the comprehensive [biography].
examples.cn: 他花了四年时间研究档案文献，才完成这部详尽的[传记]。

examples.en: Reading the [biographies] of successful individuals can provide valuable insights into persistence and resilience.
examples.cn: 阅读成功人士的[传记]能为坚持和韧性提供宝贵的启示。

examples.en: The authorised [biography] was criticised for portraying the subject too favourably and omitting key failures.
examples.cn: 这部经授权的[传记]因将传主描绘得过于正面、忽略了重要失败而受到批评。

examples.en: Literary [biography] aims not only to chronicle events but also to illuminate the creative mind behind the work.
examples.cn: 文学[传记]不仅旨在记录事件，还旨在揭示作品背后的创造性思维。

words.translation: n. 生物学\n[化] 生物; 生物学
words.definition: n. the science that studies living organisms\nn. characteristic life processes and phenomena of living organisms

examples.en: Her passion for [biology] was sparked by a documentary about the astonishing diversity of ocean life.
examples.cn: 一部关于海洋生命惊人多样性的纪录片点燃了她对[生物学]的热情。

examples.en: Modern [biology] has been transformed by the development of gene-editing technologies such as CRISPR.
examples.cn: 现代[生物学]已被CRISPR等基因编辑技术的发展所改变。

examples.en: Understanding the [biology] of viruses is essential for developing effective vaccines and treatments.
examples.cn: 了解病毒的[生物学]对开发有效的疫苗和治疗方法至关重要。

examples.en: The [biology] teacher took students on a field trip to observe freshwater ecosystems in their natural habitat.
examples.cn: [生物]老师带学生去实地考察，观察自然栖息地中的淡水生态系统。

examples.en: Conservation [biology] applies scientific knowledge to protect endangered species and restore damaged ecosystems.
examples.cn: 保育[生物学]运用科学知识保护濒危物种，修复受损生态系统。

words.translation: n. 鸟, 羽毛球\nvi. 打鸟
words.definition: n. warm-blooded egg-laying vertebrates characterized by feathers and forelimbs modified as wings\nn. the flesh of a bird or fowl (wild or domestic) used as food\nv. watch and study birds in their natural habitat

examples.en: Migratory [birds] travel thousands of kilometres each year, navigating by magnetic fields and star patterns.
examples.cn: 候[鸟]每年迁徙数千公里，借助磁场和星象导航。

examples.en: The rare [bird] species was spotted for the first time in fifty years by a group of ornithologists.
examples.cn: 一群鸟类学家五十年来首次发现了这种罕见的[鸟]类。

examples.en: A [bird] in the hand is worth two in the bush, as the proverb warns against trading certainty for speculation.
examples.cn: 手中一[鸟]胜过林中二，这句谚语警告不要拿确定换取投机。

examples.en: Deforestation has destroyed the natural habitat of countless [bird] species across tropical regions.
examples.cn: 森林砍伐破坏了热带地区无数[鸟]类的自然栖息地。

examples.en: The morning chorus of [birds] outside the window served as her natural alarm clock throughout the summer.
examples.cn: 整个夏天，窗外清晨[鸟]鸣的合唱成为她天然的闹钟。

words.translation: n. 鸟笼
words.definition: n. a cage in which a bird can be kept

examples.en: The ornate [birdcage] hung in the parlour, housing a colourful parrot that greeted every visitor.
examples.cn: 精美的[鸟笼]挂在客厅里，笼中住着一只彩色鹦鹉，向每位访客打招呼。

examples.en: Animal welfare advocates argue that keeping wild birds in a [birdcage] restricts their natural behaviour.
examples.cn: 动物福利倡导者认为，将野生鸟类关在[鸟笼]里限制了它们的自然行为。

examples.en: The antique [birdcage] was crafted from silver wire and valued as an artefact of Victorian craftsmanship.
examples.cn: 这个古董[鸟笼]由银丝制成，被视为维多利亚时代工艺的珍贵文物。

examples.en: She cleaned the [birdcage] carefully every morning to ensure the canary's living environment remained hygienic.
examples.cn: 她每天早晨仔细清洁[鸟笼]，以确保金丝雀的生活环境保持卫生。

examples.en: The poet used the image of a [birdcage] as a metaphor for restrictions placed on creative freedom.
examples.cn: 诗人用[鸟笼]的意象比喻对创作自由的限制。

words.translation: n. 出生, 起源\n[医] 生产, 分娩
words.definition: n. the time when something begins (especially life)\nn. the event of being born\nn. a baby born; an offspring

examples.en: The [birth] of modern computing can be traced to the pioneering work of Alan Turing in the 1940s.
examples.cn: 现代计算的[诞生]可以追溯到阿兰·图灵在20世纪40年代的开创性工作。

examples.en: Her nationality is determined by her country of [birth] rather than her current country of residence.
examples.cn: 她的国籍由[出生]国而非目前的居住国决定。

examples.en: The [birth] rate in many developed nations has been declining steadily over the past three decades.
examples.cn: 过去三十年来，许多发达国家的[出生]率持续下降。

examples.en: The [birth] of the environmental movement in the 1960s reshaped attitudes towards industrialisation and nature.
examples.cn: 20世纪60年代环保运动的[诞生]重塑了人们对工业化和自然的态度。

examples.en: Social mobility research examines how much one's circumstances at [birth] determine life outcomes.
examples.cn: 社会流动性研究考察[出生]时的环境在多大程度上决定了人生结果。

words.translation: n. 生日
words.definition: n. an anniversary of the day on which a person was born (or the celebration of it)\nn. the date on which a person was born

examples.en: She celebrated her eighteenth [birthday] with a small gathering of close friends and family.
examples.cn: 她与亲密的朋友和家人小聚，庆祝了自己的十八岁[生日]。

examples.en: The university marked its centenary [birthday] with a series of academic symposia and public lectures.
examples.cn: 大学以一系列学术研讨会和公众讲座纪念百年[诞辰]。

examples.en: Remembering colleagues' [birthdays] is a small but meaningful gesture that strengthens workplace relationships.
examples.cn: 记住同事的[生日]是一个微小但有意义的举动，能增强职场关系。

examples.en: She received a collection of classic novels as a [birthday] gift from her literature professor.
examples.cn: 她收到了文学教授赠送的一套经典小说作为[生日]礼物。

examples.en: The charity celebrated its [birthday] by launching a new initiative to support young people in need.
examples.cn: 慈善机构通过启动一项支持有需要年轻人的新倡议来庆祝其成立[周年纪念日]。

words.translation: n. 诞生地
words.definition: n. the place where someone was born\nn. where something originated or was nurtured in its early existence

examples.en: The town of Stratford-upon-Avon is celebrated worldwide as the [birthplace] of William Shakespeare.
examples.cn: 艾文河畔斯特拉特福作为威廉·莎士比亚的[出生地]享誉全球。

examples.en: China is widely regarded as the [birthplace] of printing, papermaking, and the compass.
examples.cn: 中国被普遍认为是印刷术、造纸术和指南针的[发源地]。

examples.en: She returned to her [birthplace] in rural Sichuan to document the lives of people she had grown up with.
examples.cn: 她回到四川农村的[出生地]，记录儿时相识的人们的生活。

examples.en: Silicon Valley is considered the [birthplace] of the modern technology industry and startup culture.
examples.cn: 硅谷被认为是现代科技产业和创业文化的[发源地]。

examples.en: The preservation of historic [birthplaces] contributes to cultural memory and national identity.
examples.cn: 保护历史名人[出生地]有助于文化记忆和民族认同。

words.translation: n. 饼干\n[化] 素坯; 饼干
words.definition: n. small round bread leavened with baking-powder or soda

examples.en: She dipped her [biscuit] into the tea and read quietly while the rain tapped against the window.
examples.cn: 她将[饼干]浸入茶中，静静地阅读，雨声轻轻地敲打着窗户。

examples.en: The artisan [biscuit] factory used traditional recipes that had been handed down for four generations.
examples.cn: 这家手工[饼干]工厂使用了传承四代的传统配方。

examples.en: She packed several boxes of local [biscuits] as gifts for her colleagues when she returned from her travels.
examples.cn: 她从旅途归来时，带了几盒当地[饼干]作为礼物送给同事。

examples.en: Digestive [biscuits] are commonly served alongside hot beverages in British offices and homes.
examples.cn: 消化[饼干]通常与热饮一起搭配，在英国的办公室和家庭中很常见。

examples.en: The nutritionist recommended choosing wholegrain [biscuits] over those high in refined sugar and saturated fat.
examples.cn: 营养师建议选择全谷物[饼干]，而非富含精制糖和饱和脂肪的品种。

words.translation: n. 主教, (国际象棋中的)象, 热果子酒
words.definition: n. a senior member of the Christian clergy having spiritual and administrative authority; appointed in Christian churches to oversee priests or ministers; considered in some churches to be successors of the twelve Apostles of Christ\nn. port wine mulled with oranges and cloves\nn. (chess) a piece that can be moved diagonally over unoccupied squares of the same color

examples.en: The [bishop] delivered a sermon urging the congregation to act with compassion toward the poor.
examples.cn: [主教]发表了一篇布道，敦促会众以慈悲之心对待穷人。

examples.en: She sacrificed her [bishop] to open up a diagonal attack that led to checkmate three moves later.
examples.cn: 她牺牲了自己的[象]，打开斜线进攻，三步后实现将死。

examples.en: The [bishop] of the diocese oversaw the construction of a new community centre for disadvantaged youth.
examples.cn: 该教区[主教]监督了一个为弱势青年建造的新社区中心的建设工作。

examples.en: In the medieval hierarchy of the Church, a [bishop] held considerable authority over both clergy and laypeople.
examples.cn: 在中世纪教会等级制度中，[主教]对神职人员和平信徒都拥有相当大的权威。

examples.en: The [bishop] piece in chess moves diagonally and can control squares of only one colour throughout the game.
examples.cn: 国际象棋中的[象]斜向移动，整局只能控制一种颜色的格子。

words.translation:
n. 少量, 马嚼子, 辅币
vt. 给马上嚼子, 控制
bite的过去式和过去分词
[计] 比特, 二进制数位, 机内测试
words.definition:
n. a small fragment of something broken off from the whole
n. piece of metal held in horse's mouth by reins and used to control the horse while riding
n. a unit of measurement of information (from binary + digit); the amount of information in a system having two equiprobable states
n. the part of a key that enters a lock and lifts the tumblers

examples.sense: n. 一点；少量；片段；adv. 有点
examples.en: She asked for just a [bit] more time to review the final draft before submitting it for publication.
examples.cn: 她请求再多[一点]时间，在提交出版前审阅最终草稿。

examples.sense: n. 一点；少量；片段；adv. 有点
examples.en: The situation became [a bit] more complicated when new evidence emerged during the investigation.
examples.cn: 当调查中出现新证据时，情况变得[有点]更为复杂。

examples.sense: n. 一点；少量；片段；adv. 有点
examples.en: In computing, a [bit] is the smallest unit of data, representing either a zero or a one.
examples.cn: 在计算机科学中，[比特]是最小的数据单位，表示零或一。

examples.sense: n. 一点；少量；片段；adv. 有点
examples.en: Every [bit] of effort invested in preparation contributes to a stronger performance in the examination.
examples.cn: 备考中投入的每[一点]努力都有助于在考试中取得更好的成绩。

examples.sense: n. 一点；少量；片段；adv. 有点
examples.en: The horse [bit] firmly at the apple held out by the young child visiting the riding stable.
examples.cn: 马儿大口[咬着]前来参观马厩的小孩伸出的苹果。

words.translation: n. 咬, 一口\nv. 咬, 刺痛, 穿透
words.definition:
n. a wound resulting from biting by an animal or a person
n. a light informal meal
n. (angling) an instance of a fish taking the bait
n. the act of gripping or chewing off with the teeth and jaws

examples.en: She took a large [bite] of the apple and chewed slowly, savouring the crisp, sweet flavour.
examples.cn: 她大[咬]了一口苹果，慢慢咀嚼，细细品味那清脆甜美的味道。

examples.en: The mosquito [bite] on her arm became swollen and itchy by the following morning.
examples.cn: 手臂上的蚊子[叮咬]处到第二天早晨变得肿胀发痒。

examples.en: New regulations often [bite] hardest on small businesses that lack resources to adapt quickly.
examples.cn: 新法规往往对缺乏快速适应资源的小企业[影响]最为严重。

examples.en: The cold winter air [bit] at their faces as they crossed the exposed mountain pass at dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明时分穿越暴露的山口时，寒冷的冬日空气[刺咬]着他们的脸。

examples.en: Don't [bite] off more than you can chew; taking on too many projects leads to poor quality in all of them.
examples.cn: 不要[贪多嚼不烂]；承担太多项目会导致每一项的质量都下降。

words.translation: a. 苦的, 痛苦的, 怀恨的\nadv. 刺骨\nv. (使)变苦
words.definition:
n. English term for a dry sharp-tasting ale with strong flavor of hops (usually on draft)
n. the taste experience when quinine or coffee is taken into the mouth
v. make bitter
s. very difficult to accept or bear

words.translation: n. 黑色, 黑颜料\na. 黑色的
words.definition:
n. the quality or state of the achromatic color of least lightness (bearing the least resemblance to white)
n. British chemist who identified carbon dioxide and who formulated the concepts of specific heat and latent heat (1728-1799)
n. popular child actress of the 1930's (born in 1928)
n. a person with dark skin who comes from Africa (or whose ancestors came from Africa)

words.translation: n. 黑板
words.definition: n. sheet of slate; for writing with chalk

words.translation: n. 过失, 责备\nvt. 责备, 归咎于

n. a reproach for some lapse or misdeed
v. put or pin the blame on
v. harass with constant criticism
v. attribute responsibility to

words.translation:

[计] 空白
words.definition:
n. a piece of material ready to be made into something
n. a cartridge containing an explosive charge but no bullet
v. keep the opposing (baseball) team from winning
s. (of a surface) not written or printed on

words.translation: n. 毛毯, 毯子\nvt. 掩盖, 覆盖\na. 总共的
words.definition:
n. bedding that keeps a person warm in bed
n. anything that covers
n. a layer of lead surrounding the highly reactive core of a nuclear reactor
v. cover as if with a blanket

words.translation: vi. 流血, 悲痛, 渗出\nvt. 使出血, 榨取

words.translation: vt. 祝福, 祈佑, 使神圣化
words.definition: v. give a benediction to\nv. confer prosperity or happiness on\nv. make the sign of the cross over someone in order to call on God for protection; consecrate

words.translation:
n. 蒙蔽物, 窗帘
a. 盲目的, 瞎的, 不加思考的
vt. 使失明, 蒙蔽, 遮暗
adv. 盲目地
words.definition:
n. people who have severe visual impairments, considered as a group
n. a hiding place sometimes used by hunters (especially duck hunters)
n. a protective covering that keeps things out or hinders sight
v. render unable to see

words.translation: n. 街区, 木块, 石块, 块\nvt. 阻塞, 封锁, 使成块状\n[计] 块, 数据块
words.definition:
n. a solid piece of something (usually having flat rectangular sides)
n. a rectangular area in a city surrounded by streets and usually containing several buildings
n. a three-dimensional shape with six square or rectangular sides
n. a number or quantity of related things dealt with as a unit

words.translation: n. 血, 血统, 流血, 气质, 生命\nvt. 使出血, 用血涂
words.definition:
n. the fluid (red in vertebrates) that is pumped through the body by the heart and contains plasma, blood cells, and platelets
n. temperament or disposition
n. people viewed as members of a group
v. smear with blood, as in a hunting initiation rite, where the face of a person is smeared with the blood of the kill

words.translation: n. 宽松的上衣
words.definition: n. a top worn by women

words.translation: n. 吹, 打击, 殴打, 花开\nv. 吹, 风吹, 吹响, 开花
words.definition:
n. a powerful stroke with the fist or a weapon
n. an impact (as from a collision)
n. forceful exhalation through the nose or mouth
v. exhale hard

words.translation:

words.definition:
prep. In the most general sense, indicating that in consideration
   of, in view of, or with reference to, which anything is done or takes
   place.
prep. Indicating the antecedent cause or occasion of an action;
   the motive or inducement accompanying and prompting to an act or state;
   the reason of anything; that on account of which a thing is or is done.
prep. Indicating the remoter and indirect object of an act; the
   end or final cause with reference to which anything is, acts, serves,
   or is done.
prep. Indicating that in favor of which, or in promoting which,
   anything is, or is done; hence, in behalf of; in favor of; on the side
   of; -- opposed to against.
prep. Indicating that toward which the action of anything is
   directed, or the point toward which motion is made; /ntending to go to.
prep. Indicating that on place of or instead of which anything
   acts or serves, or that to which a substitute, an equivalent, a
   compensation, or the like, is offered or made; instead of, or place of.
prep. Indicating that in the character of or as being which
   anything is regarded or treated; to be, or as being.
prep. Indicating that instead of which something else controls in
   the performing of an action, or that in spite of which anything is
   done, occurs, or is; hence, equivalent to notwithstanding, in spite of;
   -- generally followed by all, aught, anything, etc.
prep. Indicating the space or time through which an action or
   state extends; hence, during; in or through the space or time of.
prep. Indicating that in prevention of which, or through fear of
   which, anything is done.
conj. Because; by reason that; for that; indicating, in Old
   English, the reason of anything.
conj. Since; because; introducing a reason of something before
   advanced, a cause, motive, explanation, justification, or the like, of
   an action related or a statement made. It is logically nearly
   equivalent to since, or because, but connects less closely, and is
   sometimes used as a very general introduction to something suggested by
   what has gone before.
n. One who takes, or that which is said on, the affrimative side;
   that which is said in favor of some one or something; -- the antithesis
   of against, and commonly used in connection with it.

words.translation: prep. 的, 属于
words.definition:
prep. In a general sense, from, or out from; proceeding from;
   belonging to; relating to; concerning; -- used in a variety of
   applications; as:
prep. Denoting that from which anything proceeds; indicating
   origin, source, descent, and the like; as, he is of a race of kings; he
   is of noble blood.
prep. Denoting possession or ownership, or the relation of subject
   to attribute; as, the apartment of the consul: the power of the king; a
   man of courage; the gate of heaven.
prep. Denoting the material of which anything is composed, or that
   which it contains; as, a throne of gold; a sword of steel; a wreath of
   mist; a cup of water.
prep. Denoting part of an aggregate or whole; belonging to a
   number or quantity mentioned; out of; from amongst; as, of this little
   he had some to spare; some of the mines were unproductive; most of the
   company.
prep. Denoting that by which a person or thing is actuated or
   impelled; also, the source of a purpose or action; as, they went of
   their own will; no body can move of itself; he did it of necessity.
prep. Denoting reference to a thing; about; concerning; relating
   to; as, to boast of one's achievements.
prep. Denoting nearness or distance, either in space or time;
   from; as, within a league of the town; within an hour of the appointed
   time.
prep. Denoting identity or equivalence; -- used with a name or
   appellation, and equivalent to the relation of apposition; as, the
   continent of America; the city of Rome; the Island of Cuba.
prep. Denoting the agent, or person by whom, or thing by which,
   anything is, or is done; by.
prep. Denoting relation to place or time; belonging to, or
   connected with; as, men of Athens; the people of the Middle Ages; in
   the days of Herod.
prep. Denoting passage from one state to another; from.
prep. During; in the course of.

words.translation: aux. 将
words.definition:
v. i. & auxiliary. To owe; to be under obligation for.
v. i. & auxiliary. To be obliged; must.
v. i. & auxiliary. As an auxiliary, shall indicates a duty or
   necessity whose obligation is derived from the person speaking; as, you
   shall go; he shall go; that is, I order or promise your going. It thus
   ordinarily expresses, in the second and third persons, a command, a
   threat, or a promise. If the auxillary be emphasized, the command is
   made more imperative, the promise or that more positive and sure. It is
   also employed in the language of prophecy; as, "the day shall come when
   . . . , " since a promise or threat and an authoritative prophecy
   nearly coincide in significance. In shall with the first person, the
   necessity of the action is sometimes implied as residing elsewhere than
   in the speaker; as, I shall suffer; we shall see; and there is always a
   less distinct and positive assertion of his volition than is indicated
   by will. "I shall go" implies nearly a simple futurity; more exactly, a
   foretelling or an expectation of my going, in which, naturally enough,
   a certain degree of plan or intention may be included; emphasize the
   shall, and the event is described as certain to occur, and the
   expression approximates in meaning to our emphatic "I will go." In a
   question, the relation of speaker and source of obligation is of course
   transferred to the person addressed; as, "Shall you go?" (answer, "I
   shall go"); "Shall he go?" i. e., "Do you require or promise his
   going?" (answer, "He shall go".) The same relation is transferred to
   either second or third person in such phrases as "You say, or think,
   you shall go;" "He says, or thinks, he shall go." After a conditional
   conjunction (as if, whether) shall is used in all persons to express
   futurity simply; as, if I, you, or he shall say they are right. Should
   is everywhere used in the same connection and the same senses as shall,
   as its imperfect. It also expresses duty or moral obligation; as, he
   should do it whether he will or not. In the early English, and hence in
   our English Bible, shall is the auxiliary mainly used, in all the
   persons, to express simple futurity. (Cf. Will, v. t.) Shall may be
   used elliptically; thus, with an adverb or other word expressive of
   motion go may be omitted.

words.definition:
pron., a., conj., &  As a demonstrative pronoun (pl. Those),
   that usually points out, or refers to, a person or thing previously
   mentioned, or supposed to be understood. That, as a demonstrative, may
   precede the noun to which it refers; as, that which he has said is
   true; those in the basket are good apples.
pron., a., conj., &  As an adjective, that has the same
   demonstrative force as the pronoun, but is followed by a noun.
pron., a., conj., &  As a relative pronoun, that is
   equivalent to who or which, serving to point out, and make definite, a
   person or thing spoken of, or alluded to, before, and may be either
   singular or plural.
pron., a., conj., &  As a conjunction, that retains much of
   its force as a demonstrative pronoun.
pron., a., conj., &  To introduce a clause employed as the
   object of the preceding verb, or as the subject or predicate nominative
   of a verb.
pron., a., conj., &  To introduce, a reason or cause; --
   equivalent to for that, in that, for the reason that, because.
pron., a., conj., &  To introduce a purpose; -- usually
   followed by may, or might, and frequently preceded by so, in order, to
   the end, etc.
pron., a., conj., &  To introduce a consequence, result, or
   effect; -- usually preceded by so or such, sometimes by that.
pron., a., conj., &  In an elliptical sentence to introduce
   a dependent sentence expressing a wish, or a cause of surprise,
   indignation, or the like.
pron., a., conj., &  As adverb: To such a degree; so; as, he
   was that frightened he could say nothing.

words.translation: prep. 到, 向, 趋于\nadv. 向前
words.definition:
prep. The preposition to primarily indicates approach and arrival,
   motion made in the direction of a place or thing and attaining it,
   access; and also, motion or tendency without arrival; movement toward;
   -- opposed to from.
prep. Hence, it indicates motion, course, or tendency toward a
   time, a state or condition, an aim, or anything capable of being
   regarded as a limit to a tendency, movement, or action; as, he is going
   to a trade; he is rising to wealth and honor.
prep. In a very general way, and with innumerable varieties of
   application, to connects transitive verbs with their remoter or
   indirect object, and adjectives, nouns, and neuter or passive verbs
   with a following noun which limits their action. Its sphere verges upon
   that of for, but it contains less the idea of design or appropriation;
   as, these remarks were addressed to a large audience; let us keep this
   seat to ourselves; a substance sweet to the taste; an event painful to
   the mind; duty to God and to our parents; a dislike to spirituous
   liquor.
prep. As sign of the infinitive, to had originally the use of last
   defined, governing the infinitive as a verbal noun, and connecting it
   as indirect object with a preceding verb or adjective; thus, ready to
   go, i.e., ready unto going; good to eat, i.e., good for eating; I do my
   utmost to lead my life pleasantly. But it has come to be the almost
   constant prefix to the infinitive, even in situations where it has no
   prepositional meaning, as where the infinitive is direct object or
   subject; thus, I love to learn, i.e., I love learning; to die for one's
   country is noble, i.e., the dying for one's country. Where the
   infinitive denotes the design or purpose, good usage formerly allowed
   the prefixing of for to the to; as, what went ye out for see? (Matt.
   xi. 8).
prep. In many phrases, and in connection with many other words, to
   has a pregnant meaning, or is used elliptically.
prep. Extent; limit; degree of comprehension; inclusion as far as;
   as, they met us to the number of three hundred.
prep. Effect; end; consequence; as, the prince was flattered to
   his ruin; he engaged in a war to his cost; violent factions exist to
   the prejudice of the state.
prep. Apposition; connection; antithesis; opposition; as, they
   engaged hand to hand.
prep. Accord; adaptation; as, an occupation to his taste; she has
   a husband to her mind.
prep. Comparison; as, three is to nine as nine is to twenty-seven;
   it is ten to one that you will offend him.
prep. Addition; union; accumulation.
prep. Accompaniment; as, she sang to his guitar; they danced to
   the music of a piano.
prep. Character; condition of being; purpose subserved or office
   filled.

pron. 什么
interj. 怎么, 多么

words.definition:
pron., a., & adv. As an interrogative pronoun, used in asking
   questions regarding either persons or things; as, what is this? what
   did you say? what poem is this? what child is lost?
pron., a., & adv. As an exclamatory word: -- (a) Used absolutely
   or independently; -- often with a question following.
pron., a., & adv. Used adjectively, meaning how remarkable, or
   how great; as, what folly! what eloquence! what courage!
pron., a., & adv. Sometimes prefixed to adjectives in an
   adverbial sense, as nearly equivalent to how; as, what happy boys!
pron., a., & adv. As a relative pronoun
pron., a., & adv. Used substantively with the antecedent
   suppressed, equivalent to that which, or those [persons] who, or those
   [things] which; -- called a compound relative.
pron., a., & adv. Used adjectively, equivalent to the . . .
   which; the sort or kind of . . . which; rarely, the . . . on, or at,
   which.
pron., a., & adv. Used adverbially in a sense corresponding to
   the adjectival use; as, he picked what good fruit he saw.
pron., a., & adv. Whatever; whatsoever; what thing soever; --
   used indefinitely.
pron., a., & adv. Used adverbially, in part; partly; somewhat;
   -- with a following preposition, especially, with, and commonly with
   repetition.
n. Something; thing; stuff.
interrog. adv. Why? For what purpose? On what account?

words.definition:
a. Of what sort or kind; what; what a; who.
a. A interrogative pronoun, used both substantively and
   adjectively, and in direct and indirect questions, to ask for, or refer
   to, an individual person or thing among several of a class; as, which
   man is it? which woman was it? which is the house? he asked which route
   he should take; which is best, to live or to die? See the Note under
   What, pron., 1.
pron. A relative pronoun, used esp. in referring to an
   antecedent noun or clause, but sometimes with reference to what is
   specified or implied in a sentence, or to a following noun or clause
   (generally involving a reference, however, to something which has
   preceded). It is used in all numbers and genders, and was formerly used
   of persons.
